question: Which acquisition channels bring the most valuable customers?
interpretation: Traffic source is a customer attribute and aggregate-only. Value per channel is spend per buyer, not total revenue, because large channels dominate totals. Attribution is the customer's signup source, not the source of each order.
grain: traffic source, last 12 complete months, aggregate only
sql:
SELECT u.traffic_source AS traffic_source,
  COUNT(DISTINCT u.id) AS buyers,
  ROUND(SUM(oi.sale_price), 2) AS completed_revenue,
  ROUND(SUM(oi.sale_price) / COUNT(DISTINCT u.id), 2) AS spend_per_buyer,
  ROUND(COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id) / COUNT(DISTINCT u.id), 3) AS orders_per_buyer
FROM `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.order_items` AS oi
JOIN `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.users` AS u ON oi.user_id = u.id
WHERE oi.status = 'Complete'
  AND DATE(oi.created_at) >= DATE_SUB(DATE_TRUNC(CURRENT_DATE(), MONTH), INTERVAL 12 MONTH)
  AND DATE(oi.created_at) < DATE_TRUNC(CURRENT_DATE(), MONTH)
GROUP BY traffic_source
ORDER BY spend_per_buyer DESC
analyst_report:
Over <period>, <best_channel> brings the highest spend per buyer (<value>), while <largest_channel> brings the most buyers.
Caveats: attribution is signup source; aggregate-only; small channels may be suppressed.
Actions: shift budget toward channels with high spend per buyer if acquisition cost allows; acquisition cost is not in this dataset.
